audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names not one Locke ability across three prose blocks, three spikes, six wants and seven whys. It says "his R finally gives him a real kill threat" and "the Purgatory-plus-burst all-in" without ever saying what Purgatory does beyond execute. Purgatory GROUNDS. It is a 1000-range projectile that damages, slows, grounds and potentially executes.
audit.why: Grounding is the interaction that decides this matchup and it is nowhere on the page. Jayce's only mobility is To the Skies! and the Hextech Capacitor move speed on a swap — grounded, the leap is gone and the escape with it. So Purgatory is not merely "an execute to stay above"; it is the ability that removes the disengage the whole content layer tells you to rely on. The page's advice, "use Acceleration Gate to break every engage angle", is the one plan that still works inside it, and it works for a reason the page never gives.
audit.corrected: Purgatory named with its grounding, slow, 1000 range and 120/100/80s cooldown, and the consequence for To the Skies! spelled out.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer contains no cooldown number of any kind — the packet flags it as having zero sequencing cues — while the full layer already tracks Ritual Nails and calls the post-E window "the lane" without printing either number.
audit.why: Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10 seconds and it is his only way to reach you; Ritual Nails is 10/9/8/7/6s at 950 range. Those two numbers convert the page's "zero fights inside his engage range" — which is a rule you cannot actually apply, because you have to farm — into "step up in the ten seconds after he blinks". Purgatory at 120s rank 1 makes the level-6 warning a two-minute schedule rather than a permanent state of fear.
audit.corrected: Ashen Pursuit 10s, Ritual Nails 10/9/8/7/6s, Soul Ignition 18s and Purgatory 120/100/80s written into the content layer's early, mid, late and whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart reads Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Locke, Locke, Skill. The seven whys sitting under it read "Level 1 is Jayce", "Level 2 stays yours", "Level 3 is Jayce", "Levels 4-5 stay yours", "Level 6 goes even", "First item is Locke's", "2+ items reverts to skill". Five of the seven stages are labelled with a different side than the sentence explaining them.
audit.why: This is the most direct chart-versus-prose contradiction in the slice: four stages the text calls outright Jayce are drawn as coinflips, and the one stage the text calls even is drawn as Locke's. The chart is the thing a player reads on the loading screen; it should not disagree with its own caption.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 through 4-5 to Jayce and Level 6 to Skill, leaving first item with Locke and 2+ items with Skill — Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Locke, Skill, exactly as the whys describe.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core instruction is "stay above threshold" and "keep your HP out of threshold territory", with no mention of what drives him toward that threshold or what heals him back.
audit.why: Two mechanics compound here and neither is on the page. Silver Stake is on-hit magic damage that INCREASES with your missing health, so every point of chip makes the next auto hit harder — the danger curve is not linear and "above threshold" is not a single number. And Soul Ignition costs him health up front and heals a portion of it back at the end of the duration, which is a specific, interruptible window: Grievous Wounds applied before that duration ends is worth far more than the same item bought later.
audit.corrected: Silver Stake named as missing-health on-hit; Soul Ignition named with its 18s cooldown and the heal-back at the END of the duration, with anti-heal timed to it.

notes: THE INTERACTION THAT WAS MISSING: Purgatory GROUNDS. The content layer names it twice as "an execute" and never once mentions grounding — which matters more, because Jayce's only mobility is To the Skies! plus the Hextech Capacitor move speed on a swap, and grounding removes both. The page's own advice to "use Acceleration Gate to break every engage angle" happens to be correct precisely because the Gate is a ground-immune tool, and the page never says so. Also added: Silver Stake is on-hit magic damage that INCREASES with the target's missing health, so the page's repeated "stay above threshold" is a curve, not a line — and Soul Ignition costs him health up front and heals a portion back only at the END of its duration, which is a specific interruptible window that makes Grievous Wounds timing matter rather than just Grievous Wounds. Cooldowns added (the content layer had none — packet flagged zero sequencing cues): Ashen Pursuit 10s flat, Ritual Nails 10/9/8/7/6s at 950, Soul Ignition 18/17/16/15/14s, Purgatory 120/100/80s at 1000. LEVEL CHART: five of seven stages were labelled with a different side than the why explaining them — whys[0] through whys[3] say "Level 1 is Jayce / Level 2 stays yours / Level 3 is Jayce / Levels 4-5 stay yours" above four Skill markers, and whys[4] says "Level 6 goes even" above a Locke marker. Corrected to Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Locke/Skill.
